To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
angiotensins and active phorbols induce proto-oncogenes in isolated rat hepatocites.
angiotensins II and III induce c-fos expression in isolated hepatocytes and that this effect requires protein synthesis but not de novo transcription.
the calcium-mobilization hormones, PMA and angio-tensin II induce an immediate genetic response in isolated rat hepatocyte.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which hormones and phorbol ester induce proto-oncogenes in hepatocytes.
the early genetic events induced by PMA, the calcium-mobilising hormones and angiotensins in isolated rat hepatocyte and the possible role of proto-oncogenes in the control of cell proliferation.
the mechanisms involved in the early genetic response to PMA and calcium-mobilizing agonists in isolated hepatocytes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

angiotensine II, PMA and other hormones increase the expression of c-fib, c-mos and c-myc genes in isolated rat hepatocites by a mechanism which involves the mobilization of intracellular calcium, protein phosphorylation and the activation of proto-oncogene transcription.
PMA and angio- tensin II increase the expression of proto-oncogenes in isolated rat hepatocyte cultures.
PMA and calcium-mobilizing agonists increase the expression of c-fon, c-mos and c-myc in isolated rat hepatocyte.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PMA and calcium-mobilizing agonists increase proto-oncogene (c-fos and c-myc) expression and beta-actine expression by increasing the rate of transcription and the stability of the mRNA.

PMA, angioensin II, and other calcium mobilizing hormones stimulate the expression of the proto-oncoproteins in isolated rat hepatocyte, and that this effect may be mediated through the activation of the protein kinase C pathway.
PMA, ang II and other calcium-mobilising hormones induce a rapid and transient increase in c-fos expression in isolated rat liver cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the calcium-mobilization pathway is involved in proto-oncogene regulation in hepatocytes.
the effect of angiotension II on proto-oncogene transcription is mediated by AT1 receptors and is not dependent on protein synthesis.
PMA, angio-tensin II and other calcium-mobilising hormones induce proto-oncogenes expression in hepatocytes and that this effect is not shared by other hormones such as TSH and insulin.
